data.why: The app has no example analysis folder or upload mechanism of its own — it is a review workbench over a folder of its own data files (study.yaml/codebook.yaml/extracts.jsonl/themes.yaml) that only ta.py may write, so a small but complete three-participant pilot study (two coded transcripts, one deliberately left uncoded, a partially built codebook with two accepted and two candidate codes, one theme with a tension and one theme still awaiting claims, and two pending agent proposals in the inbox) was authored by hand to match the schema in references/data-model.md exactly, including verbatim extract text at the correct transcript line numbers so ta.py's verify/validate checks pass.

goals: Review the agent's coding of a transcript against the codebook (spans, extract chips, kinds) and accept or correct it
Decide which candidate codes earn a place in the codebook, reading the extracts and the agent's proposal/why behind each
Resolve the agent's staged proposals in the inbox (a merge-code suggestion, a comment thread) by accepting, rejecting, or replying
Organize codes into themes on the board, write a theme's brief, and judge which codes and claims the agent proposes for it
Check coverage across participants and codes (n/N) so a prevalence claim rests on a full pass rather than the most quotable participants
Select and verify verbatim quotes for a results section, respecting said/did/intent distinctions

review.summary: The tree is a faithful, well-evidenced map of the reviewing half of this workbench: its phases follow the README's stages, the labels are clear, and the 9 screens I checked support their nodes. It needs fixes before filing: the core of theme building (grouping codes into themes, judging the agent's proposals for a theme) and codebook restructuring are missing, t16 needs splitting, and quote reordering is shown as working when the replay found it does not stick.
